name: Graph neural networks
title: Graph neural networks: the family the paper's layer belongs to
blurb: A hypergraph network is a graph network with the pairwise assumption relaxed, so the family tree comes first. This section builds the message-passing recipe that nearly every graph network instantiates, then walks the four that define the lineage — GCN's normalised aggregation, GAT's learned attention, GraphSAGE's inductive sampling, and GIN's expressiveness question — and closes on what changes when a single relation has many members rather than two.
skip_hint: If you can write the message-passing update from memory and say what a sum aggregator distinguishes that a mean aggregator cannot, skip this section.
